card.statement: At a fixed, validated Humming GEMM selection, test per-token FP8 activations against BF16 while retaining native MXFP4 weights. This isolates activation traffic and arithmetic from backend selection. #59488 describes enforcing and logging the requested schema, while #60600 reports that installed Humming 0.1.16 rejects block-FP8/MXFP4 and can silently substitute per-token FP8 when fallback is allowed. Consequently, #61875's block-FP8 claim cannot justify enabling that format here. The transfer hypothesis is that per-token FP8 saves more expert work than quantization adds at the target's full-size EP4 experts. Establish named-format support or an equivalent verified configuration first; target quality, routed-MoE benefit, and effect size remain unknown.

credible_improvement_required.rationale: Reducing activation traffic and changing expert arithmetic is a credible mechanism, with quantization overhead as a competing cost. Fixed-Humming BF16 versus verified per-token FP8 isolates the precision delta, while retaining MARLIN and the best static backend prevents a misleading local win. The explicit schema inspection addresses unresolved baseline support.

Proposed scale, clipping, graph and quality checks are suitable but not completed evidence.

Its dependency on the backend experiment should prevent duplicate setup and premature implementation.

card.statement: Port #61461's SM90 launch configuration for the delayed fused mHC post/pre-norm operation only in its supported one-to-eight-token band. The installed selector uses a GB300-derived configuration; for H5120 and confirmed hc_mult=4, the patch selects (12,10,256) instead of (2,8,128). Fewer projection tiles reduce repeated post-mapping work, offering a plausible latency saving when these launches are exposed. The author reports H20 operator improvements and a small low-concurrency serving gain, but no H200 measurement and no separated C64 gain. Count actual eligible kernel calls before porting: seq64 and DSpark k5 do not establish small-token occupancy. Retain the existing selection outside the band and evaluate this independently of coefficient overlap.

credible_improvement_required.rationale: The installed selector and supplied patch establish a concrete configuration delta. Fewer projection tiles can reduce repeated post-mapping work. The unchanged synchronous configuration is the appropriate simple comparator, and counting actual small-token calls can cheaply determine whether the mechanism matters to primary traffic.

Numerical, warmup, replay and fallback checks are well scoped; the application check excludes tests and native dependencies.

card.statement: Test the existing mHC coefficient-stream overlap design on SM90 through an explicit opt-in, after repairing and validating any executed TF32 prenorm path. Installed source excludes SM90, while #60768 describes a constrained opt-in with CPU dispatch tests only. The proposed performance mechanism is to hide independent coefficient work behind other GPU work; at TP1, it cannot claim a fused TP all-reduce saving. First establish a legal overlap window and compare against the best validated synchronous fused mHC configuration. card.statement: Investigate an opt-in native-MXFP4 FlashInfer MegaMoE adapter for each EP4 replica, with an eligibility check before implementation. #6517 describes SM90 FP4 kernels, checkpoint-layout requirements, and a workspace cleanup repair; its H200 push gains concern EP8 plans and do not transfer here. #62603 supplies complementary evidence that fused dispatch, expert computation, and combine can help eligible FP8 workloads, but it is not a native-MXFP4 V4.1 integration. The transfer hypothesis is that fusion reduces exposed communication and staging relative to the best validated static backend. Require exact E384/H5120/I2304/top6 support, swiglu_limit10, legal EP4 plans, and globally consistent workspace sizing. If these cannot be established, defer the port; do not substitute converted FP8 weights or an unclamped activation.

credible_improvement_required.rationale: Fusing dispatch, expert computation and combine can remove staging and launch overhead relative to the supplied separate expert path. The proposed eligibility review is concrete and precedes implementation. Comparing against the best validated static backend is appropriate; exposed communication cost and target gains remain unknown.

h200_applicability_and_correctness_requi.rationale: Exact FlashInfer FP4 API availability, plan legality, scale conversion and swiglu_limit10 behavior are unresolved on 0.7.0.post1. Supplied DeepGEMM #411/#473 patches provide additional SM90 paths whose visible dimensional checks admit the target geometry, but the excerpts do not establish clamp semantics or complete eligibility. These are gaps, not demonstrated incompatibility.

discriminating_experiment.rationale: The plan covers fused-call opportunities, per-group capacity agreement, valid/processed tokens, memory/KV loss, idle ranks, skew and held-out capacity boundaries. Dependency-matched controls are valuable. However, matching native weights alone does not isolate fusion if activation quantization, scale granularity or rounding also changes.

traceable_engineering_support.rationale: #6517 supplies a concrete cleanup failure and author-reported tests, but its implementation patch is unavailable. Its H200 push claim explicitly leaves "H20 and EP4 plans unchanged." #62603 concerns block-FP8 weights and GLM serving, including low-load TTFT and oversized-workspace regressions. These reports motivate the adapter; they do not establish native-MXFP4 V4.1 behavior.

practical_value_and_portfolio_coverage.rationale: Fusion adds communication and staging coverage beyond expert GEMM tuning, but has the highest and currently unknown integration cost. Eligibility-first stopping and fixed initial plans contain scope. Workspace duplication, KV loss and low-load tails could erase value, so this is a conditional port investigation rather than a ready serving experiment.

objections: Scope the SM100 restriction to the integrated vLLM backend described by #62603. Supplied DeepGEMM #411/#473 contain SM90 implementation paths and deserve an explicit eligibility comparison.
E384/EP4 divisibility and passing visible dimension checks do not establish clamped SwiGLU, scale representability, complete planner legality or graph safety.
A faster fused arm could reflect changed activation arithmetic or weight-scale conversion. The current experiment does not fully isolate those effects from fusion.
